items.entity: Cubic design domain (40×40×40 voxels): physical edge length / voxel size
items.description: 'Structures optimization' says only that the design domain is divided into 40×40×40 voxels. The physical size used in the finite-element analysis is never given. The SDF network and dataset are defined on the unit cube [0,1]^3 ('Model architecture'; Methods 'Loss function and training'), which suggests an edge of 1. However, FE codes that use one unit per voxel are just as common. The compliance values in Fig. 7c depend on this choice; the cubic shape does not.
readings: Unit cube, edge 1.0 (voxel size 0.025)
Edge 40 in voxel units (element size 1)

items.entity: Fixed supports at the base (bottom face)
items.description: 'As shown on the right of Fig. 6, the points at the base of the design domain are fixed' ('Structures optimization'). The text doesn't say which base points (all bottom-face nodes or only some) or which degrees of freedom are restrained. Those details are only in the unseen Fig. 6 (right).
readings: All nodes on the bottom face clamped (ux = uy = uz = 0)
Bottom-face nodes restrained only vertically (roller), plus minimal in-plane restraints to remove rigid-body modes
Only the bottom-face nodes touching solid material (or the discrete points drawn in Fig. 6) are fixed

items.entity: Four lateral (side) faces of the cubic cell
items.description: 'Structures optimization' / Fig. 6 describe only the fixed base and the loaded top. Nothing is said about the side faces. The cell is a unit cell that is later repeated periodically in the printed scaffold (Fig. 9 text), so periodic or symmetry conditions are plausible alternatives to free faces.
readings: Lateral faces traction-free
Periodic boundary conditions between opposite lateral faces
Symmetry/roller conditions (zero normal displacement) on the lateral faces

items.entity: Distributed compressive load on the top surface via a 'thin shell'
items.description: 'the top surface is subjected to distributed forces generated by placing a thin shell at the top of the design domain' ('Structures optimization'; shown only in Fig. 6 right). The text doesn't say how the force is spread over the nodes (pressure with consistent weights or equal point loads), which nodes carry it, or whether the loading is force- or displacement-controlled.
readings: Uniform pressure over the whole top face of the shell, as consistent nodal loads (corner/edge/interior weights 1/4, 1/2, 1)
Equal point forces on every top-surface node
Forces applied only to top-surface nodes of solid elements
Prescribed uniform downward displacement of the shell (displacement-controlled rigid-plate compression)

items.entity: Magnitude of the top compressive load
items.description: No force or pressure value is given anywhere ('Structures optimization', Fig. 6). The compliance values in Fig. 7c (and 0.2798 etc. for Fig. 9) depend on it. The optimization uses the normalized c/c0, so the layout does not.
readings: Total force 1.0 spread over the top face
Unit force at each top-face node (total 41 × 41 = 1681)
Unit pressure on the top face (total force = face area: 1 for the unit cube, 1600 in voxel units)

items.entity: Thin load-distributing shell at the top of the domain
items.description: The 'thin shell' ('Structures optimization'; Fig. 6 right) has no stated thickness or stiffness. It is also unclear whether it occupies the top voxel layer(s) of the 40×40×40 grid or is added above it. That also decides whether the network's unit cube maps onto 40 or 39 designable layers, and whether the shell is a non-design solid region at all.
readings: One voxel layer (1/40 of the edge) of fixed solid (rho = 1, E = 1) occupying the top layer of the 40×40×40 grid (39 designable layers)
One voxel layer of fixed solid added above the 40×40×40 design grid (mesh 40×40×41)
A thicker fixed-solid layer of 2–3 voxels
A quasi-rigid plate (much stiffer than E = 1) or shell elements instead of ordinary solid voxels
No physical layer: the 'shell' only means the load is spread over all top-face nodes

items.entity: Volume accounting of the top shell in V and V0
items.description: The volume is V = sum of rho_e v_e with V0 set from the target VF ('Structures optimization'; Eq. 22). The text doesn't say whether the shell's solid material counts toward V, or whether VF refers to the design region or the whole mesh.
readings: Shell excluded: V counts designable voxels only, V0 = VF × design-region volume
Shell included: V counts all voxels, V0 = VF × total mesh volume

items.entity: How the volume constraint is enforced
items.description: 'Structures optimization' and Eq. (22) state an inequality V <= V0. The actual optimization instead uses the two-sided soft penalty mu(V/V0 - 1)^2 (Eq. 23), with mu ramped from 10 to 500. That pushes V toward V0 from both sides and only approximately, so the final VF may differ slightly from the target (Fig. 7e).
readings: Hard inequality V <= V0 (OC/MMA style)
Hard equality V = V0
Soft penalty mu(V/V0 - 1)^2 as in Eq. (23), mu = 10 increasing by 1 per iteration up to 500

items.entity: Penalization exponent p of the Young's modulus interpolation
items.description: 'Structures optimization' says E comes from 'p-norm weighted interpolation' between Emax = 1.0 and Emin = 1e-3 but gives no value of p. Eq. (12) only says p 'is set as 3 in most cases', and that is in the generic SIMP description, not the pattern-preserving method.
readings: p = 1 (linear interpolation, relying on the projection for 0/1 densities)
Continuation from p = 1 to p = 3

items.description: 'Structures optimization' says the SDF values 'are filtered and projected'. The pattern-preserving method (Methods, Eqs. 15–16 and 22) defines only the two projections, though. The density filter of Eqs. (13)–(14) appears only in the generic SIMP description, and its radius r_d is never given.
readings: No filter; only the SDF projections of Eqs. (15)–(16)
Linear (hat) density filter of Eqs. (13)–(14) with r = 1.5 voxels
Same filter with r = 2 voxels
Same filter with r = 3 voxels

items.description: Eq. (15) gives rho_bar = (e^{-alpha s} - 1)(e^{alpha s} + 1). That is unbounded, so after Eq. (16) the density falls outside [0,1]. The system after Eq. (17) (labelled Eq. 22) gives rho_bar = e^{alpha s} - 1, which maps inside points (s < 0) to void. That contradicts the statement that elements with f <= 0 are solid. The bounded form (e^{-alpha s} - 1)/(e^{-alpha s} + 1) is probably what was meant.
readings: rho_bar = (e^{-alpha s} - 1)/(e^{-alpha s} + 1) = tanh(-alpha s/2) (bounded in [-1,1], solid where s <= 0)
rho_bar = (e^{-alpha s} - 1)(e^{alpha s} + 1), literally Eq. (15)
rho_bar = e^{alpha s} - 1, literally Eq. (22) (solid/void inverted)
rho_bar = e^{-alpha s} - 1 (Eq. (22) with the sign fixed)

items.entity: beta continuation of the tanh projection (Eq. 16)
items.description: Methods 'Pattern-preserving TO framework': 'we start from beta = 1.0 and increase its value by beta = 4.0 after every 30 iterations until it reaches 128'. It isn't clear whether the increase is added, multiplied, or something else. The text also says the 'bumps' in Fig. 7d–e come from these beta changes.
readings: Multiply by 4 every 30 iterations: 1, 4, 16, 64, then 128 (capped)
Add 4 every 30 iterations: 1, 5, 9, …, 125, then 128
Double every 30 iterations: 1, 2, 4, …, 128
Jump to 4 after 30 iterations, then double every 30 iterations up to 128

items.entity: Adam optimizer hyperparameters for updating the latent code
items.description: Methods 'Pattern-preserving TO framework' says Adam updates z by backpropagation but gives no learning rate or moment parameters. The 5e-4 learning rate in the text belongs to network training (morphology learning), not to the topology optimization.
readings: lr = 1e-3 (Adam default), default beta1/beta2
lr = 5e-4 (the morphology-learning rate)
lr = 1e-2
lr = 1e-1

items.entity: Number of optimization iterations / stopping criterion
items.description: No maximum iteration count or convergence tolerance is given. Only the schedules are stated: mu goes from 10 to 500 at +1 per iteration (490 iterations), and beta changes every 30 iterations. The actual count appears only in the convergence curves of Fig. 7d–e.
readings: Stop when mu reaches 500 (about 490 iterations)
Stop one 30-iteration stage after beta reaches 128 (about 150 iterations with the ×4 schedule, 240 with doubling, 990 with +4)
Stop when the relative change in loss/compliance falls below a tolerance (e.g., 1e-3)
Fixed iteration count read from the Fig. 7d–e curves

items.entity: Initial structure (starting latent code / initial density field; also defines c0 in Eq. 23)
items.description: 'Mechanical stiffness' / Fig. 7a: the runs start from 'a structure randomly selected from the filtered dataset', shown only as the left-most image in Fig. 7a&b. Its TPMS blend weights w_i, solid-or-sheet type, isovalue C_d/C_t and initial VF are not given. The optimization is local, so the result depends on this start.
readings: The specific filtered-dataset TPMS shown at the far left of Fig. 7a, voxelized on the 40^3 grid (blend weights and isovalue inferred from the figure)
Uniform initial density equal to the target VF (standard SIMP start)
A stand-in single-type TPMS (e.g., gyroid or primitive, solid or sheet) with its isovalue chosen to match the apparent VF in the figure

items.entity: Design parameterization: latent-code space of the trained SDF networks (filtered vs full dataset)
items.description: In 'Structures optimization' / Methods the design variables are the 128-D latent codes of the network f_theta, not voxel densities. Fig. 7 compares a network trained on the filtered dataset (132 models) with one trained on the full dataset (1,960 models). The text gives neither the trained weights nor the 132 expert-selected models (a subjective filter over random blend weights and isovalues). It also doesn't state the training settings for the full-dataset network separately. A plain density-based solver explores a different design space and will not reproduce the TPMS-like layouts.
readings: Free voxel densities (standard density-based SIMP with OC/MMA); the layout is not confined to TPMS-like patterns
128-D latent code of the authors' filtered-dataset network (132 models), weights taken from the code repository
128-D latent code of the authors' full-dataset network (1,960 models)
Latent code of a network retrained with the described procedure on a regenerated dataset (different weights and samples)
